{{lowercase title}}
In algebra, a '''j-multiplicity''' is a generalization of a [[Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity]]. For ''m''-primary ideals, the two notions coincide.<!-- It was introduced by Achilles and Manaresi in 1993, and has an application to the study of singularities in algebraic varieties.-->

== Definition ==
Let <math>(R, \mathfrak{m})</math> be a [[local ring|local]] [[Noetherian ring]] of [[Krull dimension]] <math>d > 0</math>. Then the '''j-multiplicity''' of an [[ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] ''I'' is
:<math>j(I) = j(\operatorname{gr}_I R)</math>
where <math>j(\operatorname{gr}_I R)</math> is the normalized coefficient of the degree ''d''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1 term in the Hilbert polynomial <math>\Gamma_\mathfrak{m}(\operatorname{gr}_I R)</math>; <math>\Gamma_\mathfrak{m}</math> means the space of sections supported at <math>\mathfrak{m}</math>.
